% Realistic compile-sandbox integration fixture.
%
% Exercises four things the trivial \documentclass{article} fixture
% never did, each of which corresponded to a real shipped bug:
%
%   1. A non-article document class (IEEEtran) -- texlive-publishers
%      was missing from the original image.
%   2. biblatex + biber -- forces latexmk to invoke biber, which
%      means the $biber profile-wrapper override is exercised. The
%      regex for stripping host-path overrides was wrong.
%   3. Multiple latexmk passes (cite + ref) -- the compile takes a
%      few seconds rather than being instantaneous, so streaming
%      stdout to onOutput actually matters.
%   4. The `--` option terminator never reached here because the
%      args remapper strips it; if it ever stops stripping,
%      latexmk 4.79 (Bookworm) will reject the whole argv.
%
% Build outside the test harness with:
%   docker run --rm \
%     -v "$PWD":/workdir:rw --user 1000:1000 \
%     -w /workdir flowtex/compile-sandbox:tl-2022 \
%     -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -f --no-shell-escape \
%     -jobname=main main.tex

\documentclass{IEEEtran}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\addbibresource{refs.bib}

\title{Compile-sandbox integration smoke test}
\author{FlowTex}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This document exists only to make latexmk run pdflatex + biber +
pdflatex + pdflatex (the standard ``two pass'' resolution loop)
against a non-trivial document class inside the FlowTex compile
sandbox. The test asserts a valid PDF lands on disk, that the
.bbl carries the resolved citation, and that the compile takes
long enough for streamed stdout chunks to arrive.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
The compile sandbox runs latexmk inside a network-less, read-only,
cap-dropped Docker container per request~\cite{turing1936}. The
test exercises bibliography resolution
through biber~\cite{lamport1986}.

\section{Cross-reference test}
Section~\ref{sec:result} appears later and forces a second pdflatex
pass to resolve the forward reference.

\section{Result}\label{sec:result}
If you can read this and Section~\ref{sec:result} above resolves to
``Section~3'' or similar, the multi-pass compile worked end-to-end.

\printbibliography
\end{document}
